args.text: Give the citation for Pease v. State, 15 Fla. L. Weekly Fed. D 2949, including the court. Use the Florida form for a district court of appeal (Fla. R. App. P. 9.800).

corrections.problem: Florida Law Weekly is an advance-sheet service; cite the reporter: Pease v. State, 570 So. 2d 1116 (Fla. 2d DCA 1990) (the weekly cite reads 15 Fla. L. Weekly D2949).

json.corrections_note: Apply replace_with verbatim; re-run check_brief on the revised text.

treatment.proposition_note: No proposition-level signal for this use: no proposition data for this case (propositions cover passages other courts quote from frequently cited cases).

weekly_cite.series: Fla. L. Weekly D (Florida District Courts of Appeal); "Fed." is the federal weekly and does not fit a state decision
weekly_cite.resolved_via: reporter index (CourtListener records the weekly cite on this case)
weekly_cite.note: Read 15 Fla. L. Weekly Fed. D 2949 as the Florida Law Weekly cite 15 Fla. L. Weekly D2949, a parallel of 570 So. 2d 1116. Florida Law Weekly is an advance-sheet service: cite the Southern Reporter (Pease v. State, 570 So. 2d 1116 (Fla. 2d DCA 1990)), with the weekly cite only as a parallel where a rule asks for it. "Fla. L. Weekly Fed." is the FEDERAL weekly (federal courts); this is a Florida state decision, so its weekly cite is 15 Fla. L. Weekly D2949 (CourtListener files it under "Fed. D").

statutes.note: Statutes, regulations and court rules found in the document, checked against the corpus that holds each one (kind-scoped: a rule cite is never verified against a statute row). Quoted statutory language attached to a case citation is compared with the sections the document names (quote_checks[].statute_quote); statute text quoted under its own cite is listed as quoted_text and not compared yet.

FL-RULE.edition: Florida court rules as published by floridabar.org: the source's current rules, re-fetched on our daily refresh
FL-RULE.current_through: the rules as published by floridabar.org when last checked, 2026-10-01
FL-RULE.lag_note: Court rules change by court order, often effective January 1 or July 1: an amendment ordered after 2026-10-01 is not in this text.
FL-RULE.temporal_note: Current codification as of Oct. 1, 2026 (the rules as published by floridabar.org), not a historical version. Court rules change by court order, often effective January 1 or July 1: an amendment ordered after 2026-10-01 is not in this text. Each row's currency.last_amended_year / effective_date (when recorded) dates the section; for events before that date the text may have read differently. get_statute with as_of checks one section against the operative date.

statutes.currency_note: Each verified statute carries currency: the edition held and, where recorded, when the section last changed. A brief about past conduct (an offense, a contract, a limitations period, a procedural step) applies the text in force on that date: a section amended after it may have read differently, and an older offense may be charged under a predecessor section. get_statute or check_citation with as_of checks one section against the operative date.
